w10_T4_002439: Priya tracks her swimming in metres, converting any distance her coach gives in kilometres into metres before it goes into her log. On Monday morning she swam 8 sets of 165 metres each. In the afternoon she added a cool-down of 20 metres, and in the evening she swam another 56 metres. She repeated exactly the same Monday programme on each of 4 days that week. On the last of those days she finished the evening session with a final 10 metres of gentle backstroke. How many metres did Priya swim in total that week?
w10_T4_002448: Marta began the week with 195 dollars in her purse. On Monday she paid 125 dollars for a monthly train pass. On Tuesday her friend Leo repaid the 36 dollars he had borrowed from her, which left Leo with less money in his own wallet than Marta had in her purse. On Thursday Marta spent 76 dollars on groceries, and on Saturday she earned 25 dollars babysitting. How many dollars does Marta have in her purse at the end of the week?
w10_T4_002451: Omar bought 173 seed packets for his allotment but gave 126 of them to his neighbour Beatriz, so Beatriz then owned more packets than Omar did. Each of Omar's remaining packets was sown into 4 rows, and every row produced 3 pea plants. Every plant grew 8 pods, and each pod held 5 peas. Beatriz's allotment is 12 metres long. Omar also found 30 loose dried peas in an old jar and added them to his harvest. How many peas did Omar have altogether?
w10_T4_002456: On Saturday morning Luis's market stall opened with 150 tomatoes, and a farmer delivered 25 more just after opening. By the end of the morning Luis had sold 133 tomatoes. In the afternoon he cut every remaining tomato into 3 thick slices for sandwiches. The stall next door sold 48 melons that day. In the evening 21 of the slices were given to the staff as a snack. How many tomato slices were left at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_002457: Nadia had 19 trays for carrying eggs to market and lent 2 of them to her cousin Femi, which left Femi with far fewer trays than Nadia still had. Each of Nadia's remaining trays holds 8 boxes of eggs, and she filled them all. At the market she sold 103 boxes. A customer later returned 7 unopened boxes, and a neighbouring farmer delivered 34 more boxes to her stall. Each box contains 6 eggs. How many eggs are in Nadia's boxes now?
w10_T4_002458: Rosa's smoothie stand runs the same routine every day. In the morning she blends a dozen batches, and each batch fills 9 cups. In the afternoon she blends exactly the same amount again, so the afternoon doubles the morning's count. She keeps this up for 7 days straight. Over that week 320 cups were handed out as free samples during the evening tasting sessions, and another 264 cups were poured away unsold at closing time each evening. Her supplier bills the fruit in kilograms, but Rosa records every purchase in grams. How many cups of smoothie did Rosa actually sell that week?
w10_T4_002460: Jonah's piano teacher asks him to report his weekly practice in minutes rather than hours, so Jonah converts everything to minutes. On each of 6 days that week Jonah practised for 24 minutes. On Sunday he squeezed in another 17 minutes. When he checked his log he realised he had accidentally counted 65 minutes of listening to recordings, which do not count as practice, so he took them out. Then he remembered a 33-minute session at his grandmother's house that he had not written down and added it. How many minutes of practice does Jonah report for the week?
w10_T4_002462: Ana keeps her bead collection on strings. She had 81 strings, but she used 52 of them to make bracelets for a school fair. Each of the remaining strings carries 5 beads. She then bought a second, identical set of strings, so she had twice as many beads as before. Finally she took all the beads off the strings and sorted them into pouches of 5 beads each. How many pouches did Ana fill?
w10_T4_002464: Dev delivers parcels on foot. His app reports distances in kilometres, but Dev prefers to write his daily total down in metres, so he converts every figure. On Tuesday his route covered 8 streets with 4 deliveries on each street, and every delivery required a walk of 105 metres from the van and back. He also walked 50 metres to buy a coffee, 28 metres to return a wrong parcel, and 69 metres to find a parking meter. He has worked for the company for a dozen years. How many metres did Dev walk on Tuesday?
w10_T4_002465: Each morning at Greenfield Farm the packing crew fills crates with 117 punnets of strawberries in each crate, and 9 crates make up one pallet. Each afternoon 8 of those pallets are loaded onto the lorry. The farm keeps this up for 6 days of the harvest week. The weighing scales read in kilograms, but the crew notes all weights in grams. The farm has been in the family for half a century. By Saturday evening the supermarket reported that 18680 of those punnets had been sold, and the rest were still on the shelves. How many punnets were still unsold on Saturday evening?
w10_T4_002470: Every morning Ines bakes 230 bread rolls and adds 5 extra rolls for the staff, and that counts as one batch. She bakes 4 batches each morning and follows the same schedule on 5 days of the week. In the afternoons, some rolls are always left over: across the week 743 rolls went unsold and were given to a shelter. In the evenings Ines tallies her takings, and every roll that was sold brought in 3 dollars. Her rival Bruno, who runs the bakery across the street, sells fewer rolls in a week than Ines does. How many dollars did Ines take in from roll sales that week?
w10_T4_002475: Hana's tutor talks about study time in hours, but Hana writes everything in her planner in minutes, so she converts what the tutor says. Each week Hana studies Spanish for 79 minutes on Monday, adds 45 minutes on Wednesday and 20 minutes on Friday. She kept exactly that weekly routine for 5 weeks. Her textbook has 312 pages. At the end she added 7 minutes of extra vocabulary review and then a 35-minute mock exam. She has been learning Spanish for half a year. How many minutes of study did Hana record in her planner over this period?
w10_T4_002476: Ravi earns 91 dollars for each shift at the warehouse. He worked 4 shifts a week for 2 weeks and kept all of it in his bank account. He then paid 575 dollars in rent. His grandmother sent him 70 dollars for his birthday, and the electricity company refunded him 26 dollars. Finally he spent 199 dollars on a winter jacket. His flatmate Sam, who works at the same warehouse, earned less than Ravi over those 2 weeks. How many dollars does Ravi have in his account now?
w10_T4_002481: At the Willow Nursery one bench holds 87 seedlings in one tray and 49 seedlings in a second tray. There are 3 such benches in each greenhouse, and the nursery has 9 greenhouses, all planted the same way. A neighbour then donated a dozen extra seedlings. The nursery is 14 kilometres from town. Every seedling was sold for 5 dollars, and the till prints its totals in cents, but the owner converts everything to dollars before writing it in the ledger. A customer also left a 30-dollar tip. How many dollars did the nursery record altogether?
w10_T4_002484: Every morning at the Hillside water depot, 7 crates arrive, each holding 173 bottles. In the afternoon a second van drops off 55 more bottles, then 7 bottles arrive from a returned order, and finally 16 bottles come from a nearby shop. In the evening the manager logs the day's total and notes that each bottle holds 3 litres, though the labels print the volume in millilitres, which he converts to litres before writing anything down. Exactly the same deliveries arrive on each of 9 days. The depot has been open for half a century. How many litres of water arrived at the depot over those 9 days?
w10_T4_002485: Each day the Riverside café prepares 213 sandwiches. A supplier delivers 46 extra ready-made sandwiches each day, but 79 sandwiches are set aside every day for a catering contract and never reach the counter. The café puts the rest out for sale each day and sells out, and it does this on each of 7 days. On the last of those days it also sold a special order of 58 sandwiches for a birthday party. The café buys flour in kilograms, but the recipe cards list grams, so the cook converts. The café has been open for a dozen years. How many sandwiches did the café sell over those 7 days?
w10_T4_002496: Jamal won 225 dollars in a raffle. He first spent 93 dollars on a winter coat, whose price tag was printed in cents, though he converted it to dollars before paying. He then shared what was left equally 4 ways between himself and his housemates. Jamal spent 20 dollars of his own share on a takeaway, and later earned 31 dollars for washing cars. He has lived in the house for half a year. How many dollars does Jamal have now from all of this?
w10_T4_002497: Marco runs a small bottling plant. Every morning his line fills 8 racks, each holding 156 bottles. In the afternoon a second shift adds 76 bottles, and then 51 more come off a repair line. This same daily output is produced on 4 days each week, and the plant keeps that schedule for 8 weeks. Marco's competitor Anika bottles less in a week than he does. The plant employs 63 people. By the evening of the final day, 14988 of the bottles had already been shipped out. How many bottles remained at the plant?
w10_T4_002498: The Oakwood theatre has 238 seats, but 90 of them are blocked off for the lighting rig, so only the rest are sold for each performance. A ticket costs 4 dollars, and the box office writes its takings in dollars even though the card machine reports every amount in cents. The play is performed 6 times a week and runs for 3 weeks, selling out every performance. Half the cast are students from the local college. How many dollars did the box office take in over the whole run?
w10_T4_002499: Kim is playing a quiz game and has 205 points. A wrong answer costs her 71 points, and a bonus question then earns her 21 points. The game has 12 levels. Kim then passes through three multiplier gates: at the first gate every point she holds becomes 2 points, at the second gate every point becomes 5 points, and at the final gate every point becomes 2 points again. How many points does Kim have at the end of the game?
w10_T4_002500: Ben repairs bikes. For each repair he charges 113 dollars plus an 18-dollar call-out fee, and he saves all of it. He completed 2 repairs a day on each of 8 working days. His parts supplier quoted prices in cents, but Ben converted them to dollars before paying, and altogether he paid the supplier 1705 dollars out of his savings. A grateful customer then gave him a 26-dollar tip, which he added. His sister Amy, who also repairs bikes, earned less than Ben in those 8 days. At the end, Ben exchanged every dollar he had left for 6 arcade tokens each, for his kids' party. How many tokens did Ben get?
w10_T4_002513: Farmer Ines had 229 hens. In spring she bought 50 more, and later sold 177 hens to a neighbour. Each of her remaining hens gives her 3 eggs a week, and she collected eggs for 3 weeks. Her feed supplier lists sacks in kilograms, but Ines notes every weight in grams. She sold every egg she collected for 5 rupees each. How many rupees did Ines earn from those eggs?
w10_T4_002516: On the morning round of a television quiz, contestant Aisha starts with 48 points but loses 37 points on a wrong answer. In the afternoon round every point she holds is worth 5 points, and then a penalty takes away 36 points. In the evening final every point she holds is worth 9 points, and the closing jackpot spin makes each point worth 4 points. The show's timer displays seconds, but the host always reads the time out in minutes. How many points does Aisha finish with?
w10_T4_002521: Leah manages a warehouse that held 236 boxes of light bulbs on Monday. During the week she received deliveries of 13 boxes, then 49 boxes, and then 35 boxes. Her colleague Marcus, who manages the warehouse next door, received fewer boxes that week than Leah did. Every box contains 8 bulbs. On Friday Leah shipped out 1463 bulbs to a hotel chain. How many bulbs were left in Leah's warehouse?
w10_T4_002524: Every morning Nora's bakery bakes 92 muffins and 59 scones. An afternoon shift bakes exactly the same again, so the day's total is twice the morning's count. Each day 53 of the pastries are set aside for the staff and never sold. Every pastry that is sold brings in 6 dollars, and the bakery sells all the rest on each of 7 days in a week. How many dollars does the bakery take in from pastries in that week?
